title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1970-10-04

ai_review.summary: Fantastic performance with standout Till the Morning Comes and Good Lovin', captured on a trebly audience bootleg that suffers from hiss and stray guitar bleed.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the inspired playing – especially the rare Till the Morning Comes, a monster Good Lovin' jam, and tight China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider – making this one of the more memorable shows. The recording is an audience‑sourced bootleg; while the mix lets the band shine, it is noted as trebly with occasional hiss and an intrusive stray guitar that mars parts of the set.

ai_rating.rationale: The show receives consistent high praise (mostly 5‑star comments) for musical quality, while the recording is criticized for technical flaws; weighted average yields a solid 4‑plus rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Treble‑heavy mix, vocals sometimes low, noticeable hiss, and an accidental screaming guitar bleed that appears in the left channel during I Know You Rider/Good Lovin'.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: Casey Jones (out of sync, forgotten lyrics)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is described as intense and sizzling, with a superb jam at the end of Uncle John’s Band and a rare, emotive Till the Morning Comes that gives the show its special character.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for stellar tone and energy, especially after the drums when he cranks up his volume; stray guitar bleed is unrelated but noted.
band_member_comments.Phil: His vocal work on Till the Morning Comes is highlighted as a reason the song was rarely performed.
